newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Fidgety Australian stocks ease off highs at close.
newsitem.headline: Fidgety Australian stocks ease off highs at close.

text.p: SPI Sycom 2338 steady US 30yr (close) 7.13 +0.03
10yrbond futs 91.790 +0.020 Gold NY 351.75 Lon fix 348.84
*Stocks ease off their highs at close as investors remain nervous over Wall Street. Vol 270.77 million, value A$767.30 million, 1,051 stocks traded, 315 steady, 392 up, 344 down.

Australian stocks eased off their high's and the key index only just remained in positive territory as investors remained nervous about Wall Street, brokers said. A sharp fall in leading bank stock Westpac also put pressure on the market.
At 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was three point up at 2,355.2, about 14 points off its its morning high, but off its lows as it briefly flirted with the negative zone.
"Basically the market is still worried about Wall Street, that is the main factor - what is happening in the U.S. market," said Chris Walker, head of equities at Colonial Investment.

Westpac shares fell more than three percent after County Natwest crossed 15 million shares. Brokers said property group Lend Lease may have been the seller and may try to offload the rest of its Westpac stake.

"That stock came off aggressively this afternoon as there are various rumours that they (Lend Lease) are going to place that stake now," one Sydney-based broker said. Lend Lease owns about 65 million Westpac shares.
Brokers said Westpac was also tipped a possible suitor for regional operator Bank of Melbourne Ltd, which requested a trading halt to its shares.
Bank of Melbourne shares rose nearly eight percent before trading was halted in its shares. The bank said it would make an announcement to the market on Thursday.

Brokers said there was some arbitrage activity with investors coming in and buying the June share price index (SPI) futures contract and selling the physicals as the futures discount to the underlying index increased during the day.

The June SPI ended square at 2338 after rising 15 points at the open, but drifted back during the day and widened its discount to the physical to 17.2 points after spending most of the morning at a single digit discount to the All Ordinaries.

"It has been a very choppy day. It started off okay, came back, ran again, then came back...then the Bank of Melbourne suspension and people see a bit of corporate activity and some buying comes in and then it went weaker again," Walker said.
Mining giants CRA and BHP led the risers among blue chips, as resource issues held mainly firm on higher base metal prices. Gold stocks were also higher.

The transport sector was dragged lower by Brambles going ex-dividend, while construction-related sectors, building materials, infrastructure and engineering also fell. The bank and telecommunications sectors were also easier.

In other local markets, Australian bonds remained hostage to developments in the U.S. finishing Wednesday's session with only modest yield falls. At 5.15 p.m. (0715 GMT), Australia's 10-year bond yield was at 8.14 percent.
Late selling pressure took the Australian dollar to its lows for the day after an otherwise quiet day which saw most of the market attention focused on U.S. dollar/yen trading.
By 5.15 p.m., the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7834/39, down on an opening US$0.7855/60 and a local Tuesday close of US$0.7872/77.
